newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: OLYMPICS-MANDELA ARGUES IN FAVOUR OF CAPE TOWN OLYMPIC BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-MANDELA ARGUES IN FAVOUR OF CAPE TOWN OLYMPIC BID.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Friday the success of the Rugby World Cup and the African Nations Cup proved Cape Town could stage the 2004 Olympics.

"The argument being put forward in Europe that South Africa should wait until 2008 to host the Olympics reminds me of the argument of the apartheid regime which was that we were not ready to run this country," Mandela told a news conference.

"Three years down the line we can see how wrong that argument was. During that time we have already successfully staged world events such as the Rugby World Cup in 1995 and the African Nations Cup the following year.
"We have a clean record of being able to rise to expectations."
The International Olympic Committee will choose the host city in Lausanne on September 5. Rome, Athens, Stockholm and Buenos Aires are the other candidates.

Mandela, who was hosting a group of celebrities and business people, has strongly endorsed the Cape Town bid, saying the Olympic movement owes Africa the opportunity of staging the Games for the first time.
Sports Minister Steve Tshwete went further than Mandela in criticising the lack of confidence in Cape Town.

"This propaganda is being spread by the European media because they know that if Rome, Athens or Stockholm does not stage the Olympics in 2004 it will be a long time before the games return to Europe," he said.
